newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel debt deal -- the details.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel debt deal -- the details.

text.p: Following are details of the deal announced on Monday to restructure 8.7 billion stg of the debts of Eurotunnel SA/Plc.
The restructuring plan is to be applied to Eurotunnel's indebtedness as at October 15, 1996.
It is estimated that Eurotunnel's indebtedness will stand at 9.1 billion stg at that date.

This figure includes 0.4 billion stg of senior debt which has been and will continue to be serviced normally and is unaffected by the Restructuring Plan. The balance of approximately 8.7 billion stg of junior debt and unpaid interest is to be restructured as follows:
(billion stg)
Equity 1.0
Equity Notes 1.0
Participating Loan Notes 1.2
Resettable Bonds 1.5
Continuing Junior Debt 4.0
Total 8.7
Future interest which cannot be paid in cash is to be satisfied with Stabilisation Notes.
1) Debt Equity Swap

1.0 billion stg of junior debt is to be exchanged for units (shares) at a conversion price of 130p. It is intended that existing shareholders will be given the opportunity to participate on a basis to be agreed.
2) Equity Notes

1.0 billion of junior debt is to be exchanged for equity notes bearing an interest rate of 4.5 percent per annum payable annually in arrears unti December 31, 2003. To the extent these are not redeemed for cash, they will be redeemed with units (shares) at a conversion price of 155p on December 31 2003.
Eurotunnel will apply the proceeds of any exercise of Warrants to redeem a proportion of such Equity Notes at any time at par plus a premium.

Accrued interest as at the date of redemption will be settled in cash and/or Stabilisation Notes. The premium payable on redemption to the face value of the Equity Notes is to be sufficient to offer the holder a retrospective yield of 6.5 percent per annum.

The net effect of these arrangements is to ensure that existing shareholders have the opportunity to subscribe for a proportion of the Units which would otherwise have been issued to holders of Equity Notes on their redemption in December 2003.
Whether redeemed in Units or with Warrant proceeds, the exchange of the Equity Notes results in a further reduction of 1.0 billion stg in Eurotunnel's indebtedness by 31 December 2003.
Prior to this date, interest is payable at the reduced rate of 4.5 percent per annum.
Eurotunnel is able to require conversion of the Equity Notes at a conversion price of 155p at any time prior to December 2003 to satisfy statutory capital adequacy requirements.
3) Shareholder Warrants
Eurotunnel intends to offer its existing shareholders "free" Warrants on the basis of one Warrant for every three Units held.
Each Warrant entitles the holder to subscribe for one Unit at a price of 150p at any time prior to December 2003.

The proceeds of any such exercise of Warrants will be applied in redeeming a proportion of the Equity Notes on the terms outlined above. It has also been agreed that existing shareholders would receive a further series of Warrants on a basis of one Warrant for every eight Units held in the event that the governments of France and the United Kingdom agree to extend the current Concession.
Each Warrant would carry the right to subscribe for one new Unit at 130p at any time prior to 31 December 2001.
If such Warrants were issued and subsequently exercised, existing shareholders would own approximately 55.5 percent of the enlarged equity of Eurotunnel.
4) Participating Loan Notes

1.2 billion stg of junior debt is to be exchanged for Participating Loan Notes ("Pret Participatif") which carry a fixed interest rate of one percent.payable annually in arrears plus 30 percent of a specified measure of annual cashflow from operations to be calculated after the deduction of operating costs, capital expenditure and other debt service costs including an agreed maturity schedule.
The notes are scheduled to be redeemed by 2040.

Subject to general refinancing provisions which remain to be agreed, Eurotunnel will have the right to redeem these notes at any time at a price that provides the holder with a retrospective yield equal to a margin of two percent over the average yield on government bonds of similar duration to the actual life of the Participating Loan Notes during the period in which the notes remain outstanding.
5) Resettable Bonds

1.5 billion stg of junior debt is to be exchanged for Resettable Bonds which will bear a fixed interest rate of 6.25 percent payable annually in arrears until 31 December 2003 and reset thereafter at Eurotunnel's option for periods of two to five years at a margin of 0.5 percent until December 2006 and 1.5 percent thereafter over the then prevailing yield on government bonds of the relevant maturity.
Subject to general refinancing provisions which remain to be agreed, Eurotunnel will have the option to redeem the Resettable Bonds at par and without penalty on any interest reset date.
To the extent not already redeemed, the Resettable Bonds will be redeemed in three equal instalments between 2048 and 2050.
6) Continuing Junior Debt
The balance of Junior Debt of approximately 4.0 billion stg will remain as junior debt.
The interest rate will be fixed at 6.25 percent per annum until 31 December 2003 or, if Eurotunnel elects, at a capped rate to be agreed.
Thereafter interest rates will revert to inter-bank market rates plus a margin of 1.25 per cent per annum.

Subject to general refinancing provisions which remain to be agreed, Eurotunnel will have the option to prepay the Junior Debt without penalty at par on any interest payment date from 1 January 2004. To the extent not pre-paid, Junior Debt will be repaid according to a schedule, to be agreed, through to 2025.
7) Stabilisation Notes
Eurotunnel will have the right to issue up to 1.85 billion stg of Stabilisation Notes in settlement of any of the above interest which cannot be paid in cash in the early years.

The Stabilisation Notes will bear no interest until January 1, 006. Stabilisation Notes will bear interest from 2006 at inter-bank market rates plus a margin of 1.25 per cent and will be redeemed from 2018 to 2026 at par unless redeemed at par at Eurotunnel's option on any interest payment date prior to 2026.

In addition, Eurotunnel has obtained the right to convert the Stabilisation Notes into Units at a price of 130p at any time prior to 1 January 2006 if it deems this to be necessary for the stability of its financial position and subject to shareholder approval at that time.
8) Senior Debt
The terms of the Senior Debt and repayment schedule will remain unaffected by the restructuring plan. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
